questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The history of the university and the surrounding nature

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy I would say

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Introductory meetings, tours of the campus and city, academic support.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The system for assigning students to courses is diabolical but everything else was great

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Many different but very expensive housing options. All lower quality and more expensive than what you're probably used to in Denmark. Minimum 5500 dkk a month if you want your own room with shared facilities.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: One accommodation offered breakfast and dinner but most just has a regular kitchen.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Note that most students living in university accommodation are first year or exchange students and that most will be a lot younger than you (ages 16-21). I lived in Murano Street Student in a 5 person flat which was alright but a bit far from Uni and social and cultural places besides a football stadium. I recommend Kelvinhaugh street which had kitchens with more space to be social (couches and extra tables).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very convenient but low standards and high rent. There was no social space in my flat, so you're forced to be in your room or out. The place looked like a prison, they turned off the heating at night (even when it was -8 degrees), and the place had nothing when I arrived (not even tp or soap). If you have the guts to try and find a flat privately, there is a big chance you find something better and cheaper, despite having to worry in a difficult housing market.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There is a very easy visa registration. Very easy housing and arrival registration. Awful registration for classes. You're not allowed to register yourself in courses, but instead you have to fill out a survey with desired courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A team of 4 or 5 visiting students coordinators work their behinds off to register 6000 incoming exchange students, so obviously not a lot of help is available.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was on the forefoot and very persistent, so I succeeded in getting the classes I desired. However, I had roomies studying computer science who were forced to take history courses. Multiple people had to go home, because they couldn't get the courses they needed to.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You do not need to adhere to the "courses available to exchange students" guide. Ask the faculty if they will allow you to take the course, and then get them to sign you up.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took 4th year courses, which KU allowed me to.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Way more creative. I often had to make up my own outline and do assignments that were unorthodox. Great experience to be honest.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Good Government and its corruption.
Issues in Authoritarian Politics
Urban Economy

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: These were all great courses.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You need to buy everything for your room upon arrival.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Busses are insanely expensive - 30 dkk each way. Uber works great if you're multiple people. Airport transportation to GLA is also very expensive. Fly directly to EDB instead and take the bus to Buchanan Bus station. Saves you time and money. Groceries are only slightly cheaper than Denmark

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They have a society for almost everything. Both sport and cultural. It is the thing I will miss most about my exchange. I strongly encourage you to join a society. Note that some of the Sports clubs are quite serious.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: "night clubs" are often pubs with live music - waaaaay nicer than your Copenhagen clubbing experience. Go watch Partick Thistle - they have a partnership with the student union so you can get cheap tickets.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the highlands. Loch Lomond is right there, and a trip to Fort William to go to Glen Nevis is also great.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, besides the UK being poorer than expected.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a club.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The fact that university students are so young. It is like going back to gymnasium

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Scots are very welcoming. Ceilidhs are also so cool.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Join a society, bring all weather clothing, don't make fun of the Celtic/Rangers rivalry.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do a trip to Belfast. Its great.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Personal development and appreciating what you have at home.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being way more alone than I'm used to (I live with my partner for reference).

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
